findings.title: Interpolating before the $__range guard defeats the no-split check for range-variable queries
findings.body: runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on each target before the partition step. The subsequent querySupportsSplitting() check relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) detecting a literal $__range/$__range_s variables in the expression (see the comment at querySplitting.ts:285-287: queries with $__range must not be split because the backend interpolates $__range against the split sub-range). After applyTemplateVariables runs, $__range has already been replaced with the full original time range, so isQueryWithRangeVariable never matches and such queries are now split into per-day chunks with the full-range value baked into the expr. Every sub-request then aggregates over the whole range instead of its chunk, producing duplicated/incorrect data for any query using $__range. The interpolation must happen after the range-variable check, or the check must run on the pre-interpolation expression.

findings.title: Double template interpolation in the shard-splitting path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables(), but the resulting queries are then passed to runSplitQuery(), which (after this PR) calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() again on the same targets (querySplitting.ts:299). Template interpolation is not idempotent in general: if a variable's value itself contains text that looks like a variable reference or a `$` character (common in label-filter values, regex patterns, or chained variables), the second pass will re-interpolate the already-substituted value and corrupt the expression or step. Either runShardSplitQuery should skip interpolation and let runSplitQuery do it once, or runSplitQuery needs a way to know the targets are already interpolated. There is also no test covering this double-interpolation scenario.

findings.title: $__auto and other interval macros are frozen to the full-range value across all split chunks
findings.body: By interpolating with datasource.applyTemplateVariables before splitting, built-in macros like $__auto (and any interval-derived variable) are resolved once against the original request's range/interval and then reused verbatim in every sub-request's narrower time range. Previously the backend resolved these per sub-request, allowing each chunk to use a range-appropriate value. The new test in querySplitting.test.ts ('Interpolates queries before execution') hard-codes the expectation that $__auto becomes 5m for all three daily chunks, which codifies the behavior change; for range-sensitive macros this can change results (e.g., count_over_time windows no longer adapting per chunk). This should be confirmed as intended and, if so, documented, since it silently changes query semantics for existing dashboards.
